speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long this lesion has been present and if you recall any specific event, like an insect bite or injury, that started it?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma Gangrenosum (likely secondary to Pseudomonas sepsis in the setting of diabetic immunosuppression). The patient's history of ant bite, rapid progression of a painful ulcer, and significant comorbidities (diabetes, Crohn's, prior steroid use) strongly suggest a necrotizing infection, often Pseudomonas. Please confirm if she has any signs of systemic illness like fever or chills, and request blood cultures and a Gram stain of the lesion exudate.
